items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: Al Grey talked about being in the Basie band for a while

ctx.x: That’s my favorite kind of music now is when it’s not so organized. But I did that big band thing, I was on the road for eleven years from one band to another, and it’s kind of a freedom to get out and just play with a little small group you know, where you don’t have any real arrangements, maybe an ending now and then or how to start it, but that’s really what I like to do the most now. As a matter of fact I always did but I always got thrown in the lead trombone chair in all these bands, and some of them like…

You know we have asked a number of players about the etiquette involved, and who gets the solos you know, and is it sometimes a point of contention between players, you know like how come I’m not getting any? Al Grey talked about being in the Basie band for a while and since he was the new guy he wasn’t getting any, you know, and he didn’t like it.

Well, the leader is the one that’s in charge of who plays, you know, like, and Gene Krupa’s band, when I first joined, he was the guy that thought that lead guys could only play the lead and the second guy played all the jazz solos. And when Frank Rosolino came on the band and it was just about that time I was going to ask Gene, I would like to move over to the second chair and let somebody else play the lead, you know. And then Frank Rosolino came on and he was a fantastic player and so I stayed over there in…
